# quest-teleop

> Generic VR teleoperation for Meta Quest headsets: a native OpenXR + OpenGL ES 3 headset app (C++, no game engine,
> no Gradle; standard OpenXR, tested on a Quest 2) and a pip-installable Python library (numpy only) that streams any 3D scene to the headset, receives
> both controllers every display frame, sends haptics and text cues, shows an in-headset panel with your own
> actions, records takes, and serves a local status page with a trajectory viewer. Includes a desktop test client
> and a demo.

- Repository: https://github.com/EntangledQuantum/quest-teleop (MIT licence), version 0.2.0
- Headsets: Meta Quest headsets through standard OpenXR (manifest: Quest 2, Quest Pro, Quest 3, Quest 3S); tested on a Quest 2
- Install the library: `pip install git+https://github.com/EntangledQuantum/quest-teleop` (Python 3.10+). Commands: `quest-teleop-demo`, `quest-teleop-probe`
- Build and install the headset app (Linux, from a clone): `android/setup_toolchain.sh` then `android/build_apk.sh install`
- Network: TCP 47800 and UDP 47800-47801 open on the computer, or `adb reverse tcp:47800 tcp:47800` over USB
- Status page: http://localhost:8800 while the demo or your server runs
- Every page below is plain Markdown; the same page as HTML is at the same path with `.html`

This file contains every documentation page, in reading order. The index is https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/llms.txt.

## Instructions for agents

Setting up quest-teleop for a user, in order:

1. Install the Python library and check it: `python -c "import quest_teleop; print(quest_teleop.__version__)"`.
   This alone is enough to run `quest-teleop-demo` and check it with `quest-teleop-probe` (no headset).
2. For the headset app, clone the repository and run `android/setup_toolchain.sh`. Tell the user first: it
   downloads about 2.4 GB into `~/android-sdk` and accepts the Android SDK licence agreements on their behalf.
   It needs cmake, make, curl, unzip, zip and Java 17+ (see Install).
3. Some steps need the user in person; ask them to do these and to tell you when done: enable developer mode in the
   Meta Horizon phone app; plug in the headset, put it on, tap "USB detected" and allow; accept "Allow USB
   debugging"; turn "Link auto connect" off. Then check `adb devices` lists the headset as `device`.
4. Some steps need root: the udev rule on Linux and the firewall ports. Show the user the exact command and ask
   before running anything with sudo. Over USB (`adb reverse`), the firewall change is not needed.
5. `android/build_apk.sh install`, then `quest-teleop-demo`, then start the app in the headset (Library, Unknown
   sources, labelled "Quest Teleop"). The status
   page at http://localhost:8800 (or `curl -s http://localhost:8800/api/state`) shows whether the headset connected.
6. To connect the user's own simulator or robot, follow "Use it with your own simulator" (a complete runnable
   example is at the top) and "Recording takes".
7. If something fails, read Troubleshooting before changing anything.


---

<!-- page: https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/index.md -->

# quest-teleop documentation

quest-teleop lets you teleoperate a simulator or a robot from a Meta Quest headset without a game engine. The
headset app uses standard OpenXR, so it targets Meta Quest headsets in general; it is tested on a Quest 2, and notes
that only apply to the Quest 2 say so. quest-teleop has four parts:

* **Headset app** (`client/quest`): native OpenXR + OpenGL ES 3 in C++, one `NativeActivity`, no Java, no Gradle.
  It receives a 3D scene from a server on your network, draws it in the room, sends both controllers back every
  display frame, plays vibration, and shows the server's cues, status and buttons.
* **Python library** (`quest_teleop`, numpy only): stream any 3D scene, read the controllers, send haptics and text
  cues, show a control panel with your own actions, map a hand to a robot tool safely, record takes, and serve a
  local status page.
* **Desktop client** (`client/desktop`): the same C++ core in a window, driven by mouse and keyboard, to try a server
  without a headset.
* **Demo** (`quest-teleop-demo`): two grippers, a cube, a rope and a cloth, using every feature above.

## Pages

Read them in this order the first time.

1. [Install](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/install.md): the Python library with pip; the Android toolchain, building and installing the APK; the
   desktop client.
2. [Headset setup](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/quest-setup.md): developer mode, USB debugging, the udev rule on Linux, firewall ports, USB link
   with `adb reverse`.
3. [Quick start](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/quick-start.md): run the demo, connect the headset or the desktop client, the controls.
4. [Use it with your own simulator](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/library.md): the server API, streaming a scene, input, haptics, cues, the panel
   and actions, safe hand-to-tool mapping.
5. [Recording takes](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/recording.md): `TakeRecorder`, the file layout, the arrays, loading takes.
6. [Status page and trajectory viewer](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/status-page.md): the local web page, its data callback and endpoints.
7. [Protocol](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/protocol.md): the wire format, for writing another client or server.
8. [Measurements](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/measurements.md): latency and bandwidth on loopback and on a Quest 2.
9. [Troubleshooting](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/troubleshooting.md): the headset does not appear in adb, the app does not find the server,
   and other problems.
10. [FAQ](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/faq.md).

## For AI agents

Every page is published twice: as HTML (`install.html`) and as plain Markdown (`install.md`) at the same path.
[`/llms.txt`](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/llms.txt) lists all pages with their Markdown links, and [`/llms-full.txt`](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/llms-full.txt) has
the whole documentation in one file. Steps that need a person (putting on the headset, tapping "Allow", enabling
developer mode in the phone app) or root (udev rule, firewall) are marked as such in the pages.

## Source

<https://github.com/EntangledQuantum/quest-teleop>, MIT licence. These pages document version 0.2.0.
